newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt widens poll lead.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt widens poll lead.

text.p: The government of conservative Australian prime minister John Howard has widened its already strong opinion poll lead over the Labor opposition, according to a newspaper poll published on Tuesday.

Support for the Liberal-National government remained steady at 48 percent from the previous poll a month ago, but Labor's backing dropped one point to 34 percent, The Sydney Morning Herald/AGB-McNair poll showed.
The latest result compares with the government's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 2 national election which ended 13 years of Labor rule.

The poll also found majority support for controversial independent parliamentarian Pauline Hanson's call for a cut in immigration, especially from Asia, and her comments that aborigines receive favourable treatment from the government.
It found 53 percent of those surveyed believed the proportion of Asian migrants should be cut, while 36 percent disagreed.
Sixty two percent believed there should be a short-term freeze on all immigration, compared with 32 percent who disagreed.
Asians accounted for more than one third of the 100,000 migrants allowed into Australia in the 12 months to June 30, 1996.

But 70 percent of those surveyed believed Australia's policy of multiculturalism, which recognises ethnic diversity within a unified society, should be kept, while only 20 percent said it should be axed.
The poll found 55 percent of respondents felt aborigines were treated over-generously by the government, while 34 percent did not think so.
The poll surveyed 2,060 people around the country by telephone last weekend.
